tomato.name: Tomato
tomato.notes: Tuscan varieties: San Marzano, Cuore di Bue, Costoluto Fiorentino, cherry

pole-beans.name: Pole beans
pole-beans.notes: Climbing, N-fixer. Trellis or poles. 8 seeds per pole. Sow after last frost

corn.name: Sweet corn
corn.notes: Block planting for pollination. Three Sisters with beans + squash

sunflower.name: Sunflower
sunflower.notes: Pollinator attractor. Trellis support for climbing beans. Seeds for birds and humans

climbing-cucumber.name: Climbing cucumber
climbing-cucumber.notes: Trellis saves space. Harvest young. Italian varieties: Lungo di Firenze

grape-veg.name: Grape (table)
grape-veg.notes: Pergola at north edge. Italia, Moscato varieties. Deep roots 3m+

peas.name: Peas
peas.notes: Climbing. Italian varieties: Piselli a grano, Tondo di Provenza. Spring crop

cavolo-nero.name: Cavolo Nero
cavolo-nero.notes: Tuscan black kale. Hardy, productive. Harvest outer leaves. Frost improves flavour. Key ingredient in Ribollita

fennel.name: Fennel
fennel.notes: Florence fennel. Consistent moisture for bulb formation. Finocchio di Firenze variety

peppers.name: Peppers
peppers.notes: Italian varieties: Marconi, Corno di Toro, Quadrato d'Asti

eggplant.name: Eggplant
eggplant.notes: Italian: Violetta Lunga, Rosa Bianca. Tunisian types also popular

kale.name: Kale
kale.notes: Hardy brassica. Harvest outer leaves. Frost improves flavour

swiss-chard.name: Swiss chard
swiss-chard.notes: Rainbow stems. Cut-and-come-again. Bietola in Italian

broccoli.name: Broccoli
broccoli.notes: Italian: Calabrese, Di Cicco. Romanesco for unique heads

artichoke.name: Artichoke
artichoke.notes: Perennial. Tuscan variety: Violetto di Toscana. Produces 3-5 years

peperoncini.name: Peperoncini
peperoncini.notes: Hot chili peppers. Italian: Calabrese piccante. Dry or fresh

cauliflower.name: Cauliflower
cauliflower.notes: Italian: Romanesco broccoli (unique lime-green heads). Cool season

potatoes.name: Potatoes
potatoes.notes: Hill soil as they grow. Tuscan: Patata di Prato

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.notes: Spring/autumn crop. Bolts in summer heat

basil.name: Basil
basil.notes: Genovese variety. Companion to tomatoes. Key for pesto

chives-veg.name: Chives
chives-veg.notes: Perennial. Pest repellent. Garlic chives more drought-tolerant

strawberry-veg.name: Strawberry
strawberry-veg.notes: Alpine varieties. Good ground cover. Runners spread

carrots.name: Carrots
carrots.notes: Deep, loose soil needed. Italian: Nantese, Tonda di Parigi

onions.name: Onions
onions.notes: Italian: Cipolla Rossa di Tropea, Cipolla di Certaldo

garlic-veg.name: Garlic
garlic-veg.notes: Plant cloves in autumn. Tuscan: Aglio Rosso di Proceno

radicchio.name: Radicchio
radicchio.notes: Italian varieties: Treviso, Chioggia, Castelfranco. Winter harvest

beets.name: Beets
beets.notes: Roots + greens edible. Italian variety: Chioggia

radish.name: Radish
radish.notes: Fast crop (30 days). Intercrop between slower plants

turnip.name: Turnip
turnip.notes: Roots + greens edible. Italian: Rape di Chioggia

celery.name: Celery
celery.notes: Needs consistent moisture. Italian: Sedano dorato d'Asti

squash.name: Squash (zucchini)
squash.notes: Bush type. Italian: Zucchino Romanesco, Costata. Tromboncino for trellis

kohlrabi.name: Kohlrabi
kohlrabi.notes: Bulbous stem, crisp texture. Harvest at 5-8cm

cime-rapa.name: Cime di rapa
cime-rapa.notes: Broccoli rabe. Pugliese staple. Cut stems + leaves

asparagus.name: Asparagus
asparagus.notes: Perennial (10+ yrs). Italian: Violetto d'Albenga. Wait 2 yrs for harvest

white-clover.name: White clover
white-clover.notes: Perennial N-fixing living mulch. Good in orchards & vineyards

berseem-clover.name: Berseem clover
berseem-clover.notes: Traditional southern Italian green manure. Strong residual fertility

sub-clover.name: Subterranean clover
sub-clover.notes: Self-seeding Mediterranean living mulch. Suits dry conditions. Ideal for orchards

vetch.name: Common vetch
vetch.notes: Annual N-fixer. Classic green-manure, mixed with oats/rye. Sow autumn/spring

field-bean-cover.name: Field bean
field-bean-cover.notes: Strong N-fixer. Chop-and-drop before flowering for green manure. Hardy to -10°C

sulla.name: Sulla
sulla.notes: Native Italian N-fixer. Proven in Sardinian agroforestry. Pollinator + manure

trefoil.name: Birdsfoot trefoil
trefoil.notes: Outstanding for bees. Drought-tolerant N-fixing ground cover. Lotus corniculatus

phacelia.name: Phacelia
phacelia.notes: Fast-growing. Top pollinator plant. Chop-and-drop before seed set

fig.name: Fig
fig.notes: Mediterranean classic. Thrives on silty-sand. Brogiotto Bianco/Nero, Dottato. Multi-purpose

persimmon.name: Persimmon
persimmon.notes: Top recommendation. Deep taproot, abundant leaf litter. Kaki Tipo, Vaniglia

grape.name: Grape (vineyard)
grape.notes: Sangiovese for wine, Italia for table. Deep roots (3m+). Ideal Tuscan vineyard conditions

peach.name: Peach
peach.notes: Tuscan classic. Regina di Londa, Pesca di Prato. Late-blooming varieties for 300m

plum.name: Plum
plum.notes: European plums. Regina Claudia, Susina di Dro. Deep-rooted, good slope stabilizer

apple.name: Apple
apple.notes: Low-chill varieties only: Anna, Dorsett Golden. Mela Casciana, Rotella. 400-600 chill hrs

pear.name: Pear
pear.notes: More drought-tolerant than apple. Deep taproot. Coscia, Abate Fetel, Williams

hazelnut.name: Hazelnut
hazelnut.notes: Excellent multi-functional: nuts, slope stabilization, biomass, windbreak. Tonda Gentile

walnut.name: Walnut
walnut.notes: Juglone-tolerant guild only. Keep 15-20m from veg garden. Franquette, Sorrento

lemon.name: Lemon
lemon.notes: Marginal at 300m. South-facing wall only. Femminillo comune. Winter fleece Nov-Mar

carob.name: Carob
carob.notes: Mediterranean drought-tolerant evergreen. Edible pods. Deep root system. Not N-fixer despite Fabaceae

almond.name: Almond
almond.notes: Heat- and drought-tolerant. Late-blooming varieties: Tuono (self-fertile), Cristomorto

pistachio.name: Pistachio
pistachio.notes: Premium nut for warm sites. Grafted on terebinth rootstock. Dioecious. Pistacchio Verde di Bronte

pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
pomegranate.notes: Self-fertile. Dente di Cavallo, Wonderful. Hardy to -10°C

jujube.name: Jujube
jujube.notes: Cultivated since Roman times in Italy. Brodo di giuggiole (Tuscan liqueur). Very drought-tolerant

goji.name: Goji
goji.notes: Superfood berries. Drought-tolerant once established. Self-fertile

elderberry.name: Elderberry
elderberry.notes: Native to Italy. Fiori di sambuco used in frittelle. Berries for jams, cordials

blackberry.name: Blackberry
blackberry.notes: Native to Italy. Abundant in Tuscan hedgerows. Thornless varieties available

raspberry.name: Raspberry
raspberry.notes: Grows in Tuscan Apennines. Needs good drainage. Prefers slightly acidic soil

red-currant.name: Red currant
red-currant.notes: MARGINAL in Mediterranean — needs summer irrigation and partial shade

sea-buckthorn.name: Sea buckthorn
sea-buckthorn.notes: Actinorhizal N-fixer. Native to Tuscan Apennines. Excellent for erosion control on slopes. Dioecious

goumi.name: Goumi
goumi.notes: Actinorhizal N-fixer. Edible berries. Well-suited to Mediterranean permaculture

italian-alder.name: Italian alder
italian-alder.notes: Fast-growing N-fixer. Gully stabilization, riparian areas, nurse tree. Hardy to -20°C

common-alder.name: Common alder
common-alder.notes: Native to Tuscany. Best for wet areas, stream banks. Actinorhizal N-fixer

grey-alder.name: Grey alder
grey-alder.notes: Fast-growing pioneer. Actinorhizal N-fixer. Good for poor soils, slope stabilization

scotch-broom.name: Scotch broom
scotch-broom.notes: Nitrogen-fixing shrub. Yellow flowers. Fast-growing pioneer on poor soils

etna-broom.name: Etna broom
etna-broom.notes: Native to Sicily/Italy. Very drought-tolerant N-fixing shrub. Ideal for poor dry slopes

spanish-broom.name: Spanish broom
spanish-broom.notes: Native to Tuscany. Abundant in macchia. Soil stabilization, hedgerow, bee forage. Hardy to -10°C

stinking-bean-trefoil.name: Stinking bean trefoil
stinking-bean-trefoil.notes: Native Mediterranean N-fixing shrub. Drought-tolerant. Foul-smelling foliage deters browsers

rosemary.name: Rosemary
rosemary.notes: Perfectly adapted to silty-sand. Tuscan Blue, Prostratus. Firebreak plant. Excellent bee forage

lavender.name: Lavender
lavender.notes: Ideal for silty-sand. Hidcote, Grosso, Provence. Firebreak strip. Excellent for essential oil

sage.name: Sage
sage.notes: Drought-hardy Mediterranean perennial. Repels cabbage moth, carrot fly. Replace every 3-4 years

thyme.name: Thyme
thyme.notes: Perfect ground cover. Creeping thyme for paths. Excellent firebreak. Drought-tolerant

oregano.name: Oregano
oregano.notes: Native to Mediterranean hillsides. Pollinator attractor. More flavour with less water

marjoram.name: Marjoram
marjoram.notes: Less hardy than oregano. Sweet culinary herb. Plant in warmest spots

nasturtium.name: Nasturtium
nasturtium.notes: Trap crop for aphids. Edible leaves and flowers. Self-seeds. Prefers poor soil

calendula.name: Calendula
calendula.notes: Self-seeds. Repels aphids, whitefly. Edible flowers. Medicinal (salves, creams)

yarrow.name: Yarrow
yarrow.notes: Deep roots mine trace minerals. Attracts predatory wasps. Extremely drought-tolerant

comfrey.name: Comfrey
comfrey.notes: Deep taproot (2m+) mines minerals. Chop-and-drop mulch. Bocking 14 preferred (non-spreading)

borage.name: Borage
borage.notes: Deep taproot mines minerals. Abundant flowers attract bees. Self-seeds. Edible flowers

chicory.name: Chicory
chicory.notes: Deep taproot mines potassium, calcium. Native to Mediterranean. Edible leaves. Juglone-tolerant

dandelion.name: Dandelion
dandelion.notes: Deep taproot mines calcium, potassium, iron. Early bee food. Edible leaves. Compost activator

chives.name: Chives (guild)
chives.notes: Perennial. Repels aphids, carrot fly. Good for inner zone under trees. Garlic chives more drought-tolerant

daffodil.name: Daffodil (Tazetta)
daffodil.notes: Rodent repellent. Early spring flowers. Mediterranean-adapted needing dry summer dormancy

crocus.name: Crocus (Saffron)
crocus.notes: Saffron crocus — most valuable spice. Plant corms in inner zone. Needs dry summer dormancy

garlic-flower.name: Three-cornered leek
garlic-flower.notes: Mediterranean-native bulb. Naturalizes under trees. Mild garlic taste. Dies back in summer

fava-beans.name: Fava beans
fava-beans.notes: Heavy N-fixer. Edible beans. Autumn-sown overwinters well at 300m. Tuscan varieties

strawberry-wild.name: Wild strawberry
strawberry-wild.notes: Alpine strawberries. Woodland-edge plants. Partial shade with drip irrigation. Self-seeds

olive.name: Olive
olive.notes: The backbone of Tuscan agriculture. Frantoio, Leccino, Moraiolo. Drought-tolerant once established. Long-lived

cherry.name: Cherry
cherry.notes: HIGH frost risk at 300m. Ciliegia di Lari IGP. Late-blooming varieties recommended. Needs cross-pollination

apricot.name: Apricot
apricot.notes: HIGHEST frost risk. Blooms Feb-Mar. Pellecchiella, Boccuccia. Choose late-blooming for 300m

chestnut.name: Chestnut
chestnut.notes: Marrone del Mugello IGP. Low frost risk (June bloom). Needs 2+ varieties for pollination

quince.name: Quince
quince.notes: Self-fertile. Cotognata (quince paste). Hardy to -20°C. Good for hedgerow

medlar.name: Medlar
medlar.notes: Historically grown in Tuscany. Fruits need bletting. Medlar jelly. Hardy to -20°C

rose.name: Dog rose
rose.notes: Native to Tuscany. Rosehips for tea, syrup. Hedgerow species. Wildlife habitat

iris.name: Iris
iris.notes: Rhizomes deter rodents. Florentine iris has fragrant roots (orris). Needs dry summer dormancy

lavender-cotton.name: Lavender cotton
lavender-cotton.notes: Mediterranean shrub. Silvery foliage. Pest-repellent. Good for firebreak. Drought-tolerant

alfalfa.name: Alfalfa
alfalfa.notes: Perennial (3-5 years). Deep taproot breaks up compacted soil. Excellent for orchard understory

crimson-clover.name: Crimson clover
crimson-clover.notes: Winter cover crop. Beautiful red flowers. Also called 'Italian clover'. Sow Sep-Oct

white-lupin.name: White lupin
white-lupin.notes: Traditional Italian crop. Seeds require soaking to remove alkaloids. Excellent for sandy soils

tree-medic.name: Tree medic
tree-medic.notes: Native to Mediterranean Italy. Forage, green manure, hedgerow. Yellow flowers. Hardy to -8°C

bladder-senna.name: Bladder senna
bladder-senna.notes: Native to Tuscany. Inflated seed pods. Hedgerow, soil improvement. Hardy to -15°C

cardoon.name: Cardoon
cardoon.notes: Italian: Cardo. Grown for edible leaf stalks, similar to artichoke.

endive.name: Endive
endive.notes: Italian: Indivia riccia (curly endive) and Scarola (broad-leaved escarole). Popular in Italian cuisine.

catalogna-chicory.name: Catalogna chicory
catalogna-chicory.notes: Italian: Puntarelle. Catalogna chicory shoots, popular in Lazio. Often prepared as a salad with anchovy dressing.

jerusalem-artichoke.name: Jerusalem artichoke
jerusalem-artichoke.notes: Italian: Topinambur. Grown for edible tubers. Very hardy, drought-tolerant, spreads easily. Good for marginal areas.

black-salsify.name: Black salsify
black-salsify.notes: Italian: Scorzonera (scorzobianca). Traditional root vegetable, less common but tasty. Black skin, white flesh.

parsnip.name: Parsnip
parsnip.notes: Italian: Pastinaca. Sweet root vegetable, improves with frost. Traditional in Tuscan winter cuisine.

flowering-maple.name: Flowering maple
flowering-maple.notes: Ornamental with edible flowers, partial shade tolerant, attracts bees in Dutch climate. Needs a sheltered warm spot in NL.

saskatoon.name: Saskatoon
saskatoon.notes: Early-ripening berries (saskatoons), excellent understory tree for partial shade, nitrogen-efficient, attracts pollinators in early spring.

monkey-puzzle.name: Monkey Puzzle Tree
monkey-puzzle.notes: Very large, ancient tree yielding edible seeds (pine nuts). A novelty species for large sheltered spots in Dutch food forests. Slow-growing.

strawberry-tree.name: Strawberry Tree
strawberry-tree.notes: Evergreen with edible strawberry-like fruit (mildly sweet), drought-tolerant once established. Flowers in autumn — late nectar source for bees. Needs sheltered spot in NL.

pawpaw.name: Pawpaw
pawpaw.notes: Largest native fruit of North America — custard-like pawpaw fruit (tastes like banana-custard). Needs sheltered microclimate in NL, shade-tolerant when young.

common-barberry.name: Common Barberry
common-barberry.notes: Edible tart berries (rich in vitamin C), thorny barrier hedge, pollinator-friendly flowers. Berberis root was historically used as yellow dye. Host for wheat rust — check local restrictions.

paper-mulberry.name: Paper Mulberry
paper-mulberry.notes: Fast-growing tree with edible fruit (similar to mulberry), bark used for papermaking. Coppices well for biomass. Needs a warm, sheltered spot in NL.

carolina-allspice.name: Carolina Allspice
carolina-allspice.notes: Aromatic shrub with edible flowers used as spice (cinnamon-like scent). Excellent for moist woodland edges in Dutch food forests.

siberian-pea-tree.name: Siberian Pea Tree
siberian-pea-tree.notes: Nitrogen-fixing pioneer tree, edible seeds (like peas), great windbreak for Dutch food forests, excellent bee forage. Extremely hardy. Regular coppicing recommended.

allegheny-chinkapin.name: Allegheny Chinkapin
allegheny-chinkapin.notes: Dwarf chestnut — smaller nuts than sweet chestnut but a more manageable shrubby size for food forests. Very sweet, small nuts.

new-jersey-tea.name: New Jersey Tea
new-jersey-tea.notes: Nitrogen-fixing shrub, leaves used as tea substitute, beautiful white flower clusters for pollinators. Needs a sheltered spot in NL (borderline hardy).

japanese-plum-yew.name: Japanese Plum-Yew
japanese-plum-yew.notes: Shade-tolerant evergreen with edible nut-like seeds (crushed). Slow-growing understory tree for shady spots in Dutch food forests.

judas-tree.name: Judas Tree
judas-tree.notes: Beautiful spring blossoms, edible flowers (salads), nitrogen-fixing (Fabaceae). Needs a sheltered, warm spot in NL — best against a south-facing wall.

japanese-quince.name: Japanese Quince
japanese-quince.notes: Hardy shrub with aromatic quince-like fruit for jams and jellies. Early spring nectar source for bees, thorny barrier hedge. Very hardy for NL climate.

cornelian-cherry.name: Cornelian Cherry
cornelian-cherry.notes: Very early-ripening cherry-like fruit (higher vitamin C than orange). Excellent for NL climate. Thrives in sun or partial shade. Yellow flowers very early in spring.

azerole.name: Azerole
azerole.notes: Mediterranean hawthorn with larger, apple-like edible fruit (haws). Wildlife habitat, windbreak, medicinal flowers. Tolerates poor soil.

dead-mans-fingers.name: Dead Man's Fingers
dead-mans-fingers.notes: Ornamental shrub with unusual bright blue, edible pods (jelly-like texture, sweet). Shade-tolerant, makes a striking conversation piece.

date-plum.name: Date-plum
date-plum.notes: Hardy persimmon relative — small astringent fruit that sweetens after frost. Very hardy for NL. Excellent rootstock for persimmons. Deep taproot.

american-persimmon.name: American Persimmon
american-persimmon.notes: Very hardy North American persimmon — sweet, rich fruit after frost. Tolerant of poor soil, deep taproot for soil aeration. Separate male and female trees needed.

beech.name: Beech
beech.notes: Native beech, edible nuts (beechmast), excellent for biomass/leaf litter. Tall canopy for windbreak edges. Pure beech leaf litter is slow to decompose — mix with N-rich leaves.

salal.name: Salal
salal.notes: Evergreen groundcover shrub with edible wintergreen-flavored berries. Partial shade, acid soil preferred. Excellent low-maintenance groundcover.

chilean-hazel.name: Chilean Hazel
chilean-hazel.notes: Evergreen nut tree from Chile — edible hazelnut-like seeds. Needs a warm, sheltered spot in NL. Attractive foliage and flowers for bees.

ginkgo.name: Ginkgo
ginkgo.notes: Ancient living fossil tree with edible seeds (ginkgo nuts, after processing). Pest-free, pollution-tolerant. Spectacular golden autumn color. Needs male for non-smelly fruit.

japanese-raisin-tree.name: Japanese Raisin Tree
japanese-raisin-tree.notes: Unique tree — sweet, raisin-like edible stems (not the fruit). Drought-tolerant once established. Good for adding diversity to the canopy layer. Needs warmth for good fruit.

black-walnut.name: Black Walnut
black-walnut.notes: Highly nutritious nuts — but produces juglone (allelopathic), incompatible with many plants (tomato, potato, eggplant, asparagus, brassicas). Edible leaves for tea. Deep taproot.

juniper.name: Juniper
juniper.notes: Native shrub, berries used as spice (gin), excellent for biodiversity. Drought-tolerant once established. Two years for berry ripening.

bay-laurel.name: Bay Laurel
bay-laurel.notes: Aromatic leaves for cooking, evergreen screen. Needs winter protection when young in NL (frost-sensitive). Excellent in a warm, sheltered microclimate.

honeyberry.name: Honeyberry
honeyberry.notes: Honeyberry — very early-ripening, blueberry-like fruit (tastes like blueberry-raspberry). Extremely hardy (Siberian origins). Needs two different cultivars for cross-pollination.

oregon-grape.name: Oregon Grape
oregon-grape.notes: Evergreen shrub with edible tart berries. Shade-tolerant, winter-flowering (yellow flowers) — crucial early nectar for bees. Leaves resemble holly.

chilean-guava.name: Chilean Guava
chilean-guava.notes: Small aromatic berries (tastes like wild strawberry and cotton candy). Evergreen shrub. Needs a sheltered microclimate in NL. Excellent for jam.

briancon-apricot.name: Briançon Apricot
briancon-apricot.notes: Alpine apricot from the French Alps — one of the hardiest apricots. Small, sweet fruit. Ideal for cold spots where regular apricot would struggle. Self-fertile.

sour-cherry.name: Sour Cherry
sour-cherry.notes: Morello cherry — excellent for NL climate, self-fertile, good for processing (jams, pies, kirsch). Tart flavor. Very hardy.

beach-plum.name: Beach Plum
beach-plum.notes: Salt-tolerant, sand-loving shrub with small, sweet plums (good for jam). Ideal for coastal Dutch food forests and sandy soils.

blackthorn.name: Blackthorn
blackthorn.notes: Sloe — native shrub, fruit for sloe gin, impenetrable thorny hedge barrier. Important wildlife habitat. Early white flowers. Fruit needs frost to sweeten.

dwarf-russian-almond.name: Dwarf Russian Almond
dwarf-russian-almond.notes: Ornamental shrub with beautiful early spring pink flowers for bees. Seeds are edible (like almonds but smaller). Compact size — good for smaller guilds.

nanking-cherry.name: Nanking Cherry
nanking-cherry.notes: Early-ripening, sweet cherry-like fruit. Very hardy (Siberian origin). Ornamental throughout the year with showy flowers and attractive bark.

holm-oak.name: Holm Oak
holm-oak.notes: Evergreen oak. Edible acorns (low tannin, can be roasted). Excellent windbreak, especially for coastal food forests. Tolerates poor soil and drought.

stags-horn-sumach.name: Stag's Horn Sumach
stags-horn-sumach.notes: Red spice from berries (rich in antioxidants, lemony-sour flavor). Striking autumn colour. Rhizomatous spreader — can form thickets. All parts non-toxic (unlike poison ivy, same family).

blackcurrant.name: Blackcurrant
blackcurrant.notes: Very high vitamin C berries. Needs a cool spot (partial shade) — excellent for NL climate. Blackcurrant leaf has a distinctive aroma and can be used in tea. Susceptible to leaf spot in wet conditions.

gooseberry.name: Gooseberry
gooseberry.notes: Very hardy fruit shrub with translucent berries (green, red, yellow). Partial shade tolerant. Excellent for jam, desserts, and pies. Needs protection from American gooseberry mildew.

black-locust.name: Black Locust
black-locust.notes: Nitrogen-fixing pioneer tree. Edible flowers (fritters — the classic permaculture treat). Excellent for biomass and pollinators. Rot-resistant timber. Root suckers can be invasive.

rugosa-rose.name: Rugosa Rose
rugosa-rose.notes: Very hardy rose with large, edible hips (richest vitamin C of all rose species). Salt-tolerant — excellent for coastal hedges. Dense, thorny barrier.

wineberry.name: Wineberry
wineberry.notes: Sweet, red raspberry relative with beautiful red hairy stems. Partial shade tolerant. Vigorous grower — needs management to prevent spreading.

goat-willow.name: Goat Willow
goat-willow.notes: Early spring pollen source for bees (catkins before leaves). Coppices well for biomass. Excellent for soil stabilization and wet areas.

sassafras.name: Sassafras
sassafras.notes: Aromatic leaves (leaves used for thickening gumbo, root for tea — use safrole-free varieties). Striking autumn colours. Root suckers readily.

whitebeam.name: Whitebeam
whitebeam.notes: Edible berries (mealy but edible when bletted, good for jam). Excellent wildlife tree. Tolerant of poor soil, wind, and pollution. Beautiful silvery leaves.

rowan.name: Rowan
rowan.notes: Bright red berries for jams/jelly (must be cooked to break down toxic parasorbic acid). Excellent wildlife value. Tolerant of poor, polluted soil.

service-tree.name: Service Tree
service-tree.notes: Rare native tree — fruit must be bletted (like medlar). Tastes like spiced pear-dates. Good for adding genetic diversity to the canopy.

wild-service-tree.name: Wild Service Tree
wild-service-tree.notes: Very rare native tree — small brown fruit (bletted). Excellent timber. Good for diverse canopy. Tolerates heavy clay soil.

yew.name: Yew
yew.notes: Evergreen — excellent for shade. All parts EXCEPT the fleshy red aril are highly toxic. Valuable wildlife habitat. Extremely long-lived.

small-leaved-lime.name: Small-leaved Lime
small-leaved-lime.notes: Linden tree — edible flowers for tea (supreme bee forage). Deep taproot for soil aeration. Leaf litter is excellent soil conditioner. Nitrogen-efficient.

chinese-toon.name: Chinese Toon
chinese-toon.notes: Young leaves taste like onion/garlic — a unique culinary seasoning. Fast-growing timber tree. Needs warmth in NL for the best flavour. Spectacular autumn colour.

chaste-tree.name: Chaste Tree
chaste-tree.notes: Aromatic shrub — seeds used as pepper substitute, medicinal (hormonal balance). Beautiful lavender flowers. Needs a warm, sheltered spot in NL. Cut back in winter.

egyptian-onion.name: Egyptian Onion
egyptian-onion.notes: Perennial onion that forms bulbils at the top — self-propagating. Can be harvested year-round. Excellent for the herbaceous layer.

ramsons.name: Ramsons
ramsons.notes: Wild garlic — excellent woodland garlic for understory. Early spring green, dies back in summer. Great groundcover for damp, shady spots.

sea-beet.name: Sea Beet
sea-beet.notes: Wild ancestor of beetroot and chard. Edible leaves year-round, salt-tolerant. Excellent for coastal food forests. Performs in poor soil.

turkish-rocket.name: Turkish Rocket
turkish-rocket.notes: Perennial mustard-like green — very productive, deep nitrogen-cycling taproot. Leaves taste like mild rocket. One of the best perennial vegetables.

quamash.name: Quamash
quamash.notes: Edible bulbs (like sweet potato, roasted). Striking blue flower spikes. Thrives in moist soil. Important traditional food of Pacific Northwest First Nations.

red-valerian.name: Red Valerian
red-valerian.notes: Edible flowers and leaves, drought-tolerant. Excellent for pollinators — butterflies and bees love it. Self-seeds readily.

daylily.name: Daylily
daylily.notes: All parts edible (flowers, buds, young shoots, tubers). Very hardy, excellent groundcover. IMPORTANT: Some species have diuretic effects — eat in moderation.

musk-mallow.name: Musk Mallow
musk-mallow.notes: Edible leaves and flowers, medicinal (soothing, demulcent). Self-seeding groundcover. Attractive pink flowers.

mayapple.name: Mayapple
mayapple.notes: Edible ripe fruit (the only non-toxic part — all other parts, including unripe fruit, are toxic). Excellent shade-loving groundcover. Ripe fruit tastes like lemon-mango.

solomons-seal.name: Solomon's Seal
solomons-seal.notes: Edible young shoots (like asparagus). Medicinal root (traditionally used for joints). Elegant, arching shade-tolerant perennial.

lungwort.name: Lungwort
lungwort.notes: Edible leaves (mild, mucilaginous), early spring flowers for bees (pink-to-blue). Medicinal — traditionally used for lung health. Excellent groundcover.

sweet-violet.name: Sweet Violet
sweet-violet.notes: Edible flowers and leaves (perfumed flowers for candying and salads). Early spring bloomer — crucial for early bees. Excellent groundcover for shade.

blueberry.name: Blueberry
blueberry.notes: Needs acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5). In NL clay/limestone, use raised beds with peat or pine bark. Excellent understory shrub. Stunning autumn colour.

ground-elder.name: Ground Elder
ground-elder.notes: VERY invasive — but an excellent mineral accumulator and weed-suppressing groundcover in areas where its spread can be contained. Edible leaves (like spinach). Use with extreme caution.

anise-hyssop.name: Anise Hyssop
anise-hyssop.notes: Edible flowers and leaves (anise/licorice flavour), excellent tea herb. Medicinal (digestive). Outstanding pollinator plant — bees and butterflies love it.

angelica.name: Angelica
angelica.notes: Stems candied (traditional cake decoration), medicinal (digestive, colds). Biennial/short-lived perennial. Impressive architectural structure. Needs moist soil.

udo.name: Udo
udo.notes: Edible spring shoots (like asparagus — a Japanese delicacy). Large architectural leaves. Partial shade tolerant.

golden-saxifrage.name: Golden Saxifrage
golden-saxifrage.notes: Low-growing groundcover for moist, shady spots. Edible leaves (mild flavour). Excellent for damp, difficult areas.

pignut.name: Pignut
pignut.notes: Small edible tuber (tastes like hazelnut-flavored potato). European woodland plant. Good for the root layer.

chinese-mallow.name: Chinese Mallow
chinese-mallow.notes: Edible leaves (like lettuce, mild flavour). High mucilage content. Self-seeding annual/biennial. Used in Chinese cuisine.

lemon-balm.name: Lemon Balm
lemon-balm.notes: Edible/medicinal leaves (lemon-scented, calming tea). Excellent pollinator plant. Vigorous grower — can spread. Cut back after flowering.

sweet-cicely.name: Sweet Cicely
sweet-cicely.notes: Anise-flavoured leaves and green seeds. Shade-tolerant, excellent pollinator plant. One of the best shade-tolerant culinary herbs.

creeping-bramble.name: Creeping Bramble
creeping-bramble.notes: Excellent dense, non-invasive groundcover with edible fruit. Creeping habit — hugs the ground. Perfect for suppressing weeds around trees.

hog-peanut.name: Hog Peanut
hog-peanut.notes: Unusual N-fixing plant that produces both above-ground seeds AND underground peanuts. Edible seeds. Great for shade-tolerant groundcover.

groundnut.name: Groundnut
groundnut.notes: N-fixing vine with edible tubers (high protein, nutty flavour). Traditional Native American staple. Needs support (climber). Beautiful brownish-purple flowers.

burdock.name: Burdock
burdock.notes: Deep-taprooted mineral accumulator — excellent dynamic accumulator. Edible root (gobo in Japanese cuisine). Leaves are also edible. Deeply aerates soil.

horseradish.name: Horseradish
horseradish.notes: Pungent root spice. Deep taproot — excellent mineral accumulator. Pest repellant properties. VERY invasive — contain in a buried pot or specific area.

campanula-rapunculus.name: Rampion
campanula-rapunculus.notes: Edible root and leaves (traditional European vegetable). Biennial. The 'Rapunzel' fairy tale is named after this plant. Nice bell-shaped flowers.

common-liquorice.name: Common Liquorice
common-liquorice.notes: N-fixing perennial. Sweet root (glycyrrhizin — 50x sweeter than sugar). Deep taproot for soil aeration. Needs 3-4 years before first root harvest. Medicinal.

skirret.name: Skirret
skirret.notes: Sweet, edible roots (tastes like parsnip/carrot — medieval European vegetable). Needs moist soil. Clusters of thin, sweet roots. Hardy perennial.

ulluco.name: Ulluco
ulluco.notes: Colorful edible tubers (staple in the Andes, waxy texture like potato). Needs frost protection in NL. Can be stored for months after harvest.

hardy-kiwi.name: Hardy Kiwi
hardy-kiwi.notes: Smooth-skinned mini kiwis (eat whole, no peeling). Very hardy for NL. Needs male + female plant for pollination. Vigorous climber — needs strong support.

chocolate-vine.name: Chocolate Vine
chocolate-vine.notes: Edible purple fruit pods (jelly-like, sweet flesh). Flowers smell like chocolate. Vigorous climber. Needs male+female or just plant two.

schisandra.name: Schisandra
schisandra.notes: Five-flavour berry — adaptogenic berries that taste sour, sweet, salty, bitter, and pungent all at once. Needs support (climber). Partial shade. Famous in Chinese medicine.

red-alder.name: Red Alder
red-alder.notes: Fast-growing N-fixer. Excellent pioneer tree for biomass production and windbreaks. Coppices well. More vigorous than common alder in good soil.

evergreen-olive.name: Evergreen Olive
evergreen-olive.notes: Evergreen N-fixing shrub. Edible fruit (tart but sweet when ripe). Excellent winter windbreak/screen. One of the best evergreen N-fixers for NL.

northern-bayberry.name: Northern Bayberry
northern-bayberry.notes: N-fixing deciduous shrub. Aromatic berries for candle-making (bayberry wax). Coastal tolerant. Beautiful silvery-grey foliage.

dwarf-gunnera.name: Dwarf Gunnera
dwarf-gunnera.notes: Unique N-fixing groundcover — symbiosis with Nostoc cyanobacteria (the only known flowering plant genus with this). Creeping habit. Edible stems.

earthnut-pea.name: Earthnut Pea
earthnut-pea.notes: N-fixing perennial with edible tubers (nutty, sweet). Beautiful pink flowers. Excellent for the root layer.

everlasting-pea.name: Everlasting Pea
everlasting-pea.notes: N-fixing perennial climber. Edible young pea pods (but seeds are mildly toxic in large quantities). Beautiful pink flowers. Long blooming season.

chinese-wisteria.name: Chinese Wisteria
chinese-wisteria.notes: N-fixing ornamental climber. Edible flowers (fritters — sweet, honey-like). Seeds TOXIC. Very vigorous — needs strong support and regular pruning.

shagbark-hickory.name: Shagbark Hickory
shagbark-hickory.notes: Very sweet nuts (best-tasting hickory). Deep taproot. Spectacular shaggy bark. Excellent autumn colour. Needs deep soil.

silver-birch.name: Silver Birch
silver-birch.notes: Pioneer tree, excellent mineral accumulator (K, Ca, Fe, Mg). Sap for syrup/tea. Birch polypore mushroom (medicinal). Good for windbreaks.

field-horsetail.name: Field Horsetail
field-horsetail.notes: Outstanding mineral accumulator — highest silica content of any plant. Deep root system. Medicinal (diuretic, bone health). Very invasive in wet areas.

watercress.name: Watercress
watercress.notes: Nutrient-dense aquatic perennial green — needs clean running water in NL. Very high in minerals (Ca, K, P, Fe, S, Na). Perfect for the water layer.

black-poplar.name: Black Poplar
black-poplar.notes: Fast-growing biomass and windbreak tree. Coppices well. Native to NL. Leaf buds used for balm. Good for wet areas.

american-bird-cherry.name: American Bird Cherry
american-bird-cherry.notes: Controversial in NL — listed as an invasive species but produces abundant edible cherries (good for jam, wine). Beautiful timber. Vigorous pioneer.
